title: Reading for Comprehension
summary: Reading strategies (skimming, scanning, close reading), types of comprehension questions, finding the main idea, inferring meaning and answering in your own words.

rows: Skimming
Read quickly for the general idea: title, first and last paragraphs, topic sentences
First reading of a passage
Scanning
Search quickly for a specific fact, name, date or number
Finding the answer to a factual question
Close (intensive) reading
Read slowly and carefully, thinking about meaning, tone and word choice
Answering inference and opinion questions
Literal
Facts stated directly in the text
Who? What? When? Where? Quote… List…
Reorganisation
Putting information together, e.g. in a table or summary
Summarise… Compare…
Inferential
Reading between the lines; meaning that is implied, not stated
Why do you think…? What does this suggest…? Explain…
Evaluative
Judging the text or giving your opinion with reasons
Do you agree…? Is this effective…?
Appreciative
Responding to the writer's style and its effect on the reader
How does the writer make you feel…?

notes.title: Practice passage: The Water Tank (original text written for FreeSheet)
notes.text:
When the taps in Mamelodi ran dry for the third week, Thando's grandmother did something nobody expected. She sold her old sewing machine.

With the money, and with help from three neighbours, she bought a second-hand plastic water tank and two lengths of gutter. On Saturday morning half the street gathered to watch the men fix the gutters to the roof. 'You will see,' Gogo said, though there had not been a cloud for a month. 'The rain always comes back to those who are ready for it.'

The rain came eleven days later, heavy and sudden, drumming on the tin roof. By morning the tank was full. Gogo hung a small sign on the gate: WATER FOR COOKING AND DRINKING. TAKE ONE BUCKET. LEAVE A SMILE.

By December, four more houses on the street had tanks of their own.

notes.title: Answering questions on the passage
notes.problem: Answer: (a) What did Gogo sell? (literal) (b) Why do you think Gogo sold something she valued? (inferential) (c) What does the last sentence suggest about the effect of Gogo's actions? (inferential)
steps: (b) She thought clean water for her family and neighbours was more important than the machine; she was willing to sacrifice for others.
(c) Her example inspired others: neighbours followed her lead and also installed tanks.
notes.answer: Use facts from the text for literal questions; give reasons supported by the text for inferential questions.

notes.title: Literal or inferential?
notes.problem: Passage: 'Naledi slammed her bag down and did not greet anyone.' Question 1: What did Naledi slam down? Question 2: How was she feeling?
steps: Question 1 is answered directly from the text: this is literal.
Question 2 must be worked out from clues: this is inferential.
The clues are slamming the bag and not greeting.
notes.answer: Q1: her bag. Q2: she was angry or upset.

items: Read the questions **before** you read the passage closely, so you know what to look for.
Check the **mark allocation**: 2 marks usually need two points or a point plus explanation.
**Quote** means copy the exact words, in quotation marks. **In your own words** means do NOT copy.
Answer in **full sentences** unless asked for one word.
For true/false questions, give a **quotation** or reason if asked to prove your answer.
Work out unfamiliar words from **context** (the words around them).

notes.label: Common mistake
notes.text: When asked for **one word**, write only one word. When asked to **quote**, use the exact words with quotation marks. Points are lost for ignoring these instructions.

questions.prompt: Which reading strategy helps you find a specific date quickly?
A question that asks you to read between the lines is…
Refer to the practice passage. What did Gogo sell? (two or three words)
How many days later did the rain come, according to the passage?
Quote the sentence in which Gogo shows her confidence that it will rain.
questions.memo: ✓ 'The rain always comes back to those who are ready for it.' (1)

questions.prompt: Explain why the writer uses the word 'drumming' to describe the rain.
questions.memo:
✓ It suggests the loud, steady, rhythmic sound of heavy rain on the tin roof (1)
✓ It creates a vivid / joyful mood after the long drought (1)

questions.prompt: What does Gogo's sign tell us about her character?
questions.memo:
✓ She is generous/community-minded (sharing water) (1)
✓ She is warm and has a sense of humour ('LEAVE A SMILE') (1)

questions.prompt: According to the passage, it was raining on the Saturday the gutters were installed.
questions.explanation: 'There had not been a cloud for a month.'

questions.prompt: Do you think Gogo made a wise decision? Give reasons for your answer.
questions.memo:
✓ Clear opinion (1)
✓✓ Two reasons supported by the text, e.g. her family had water when the taps were dry; she helped the whole street; neighbours followed her example (2)
